title: Trend for Workplace Injuries and System for Workplace Injury Reporting
what_it_is: Trend for Workplace Injuries and System for Workplace Injury Reporting

sections.label: Reported workplace injuries average
sections.summary: About 12,800 workplace injuries were reported to the Ministry of Manpower each year on average over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In the last five years, an average of about 12,800 such workplace injuries were reported to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) every year.

sections.label: No widespread under-reporting evidence
sections.summary: Assessment, observation and contacts with companies and workers suggest no evidence of widespread under-reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Our assessment and observation, and also through our contacts with the companies and workers, suggest that there is no evidence of widespread under-reporting.

sections.label: Workers reporting injuries directly
sections.summary: In the last year, close to 1,900 workers reported their injuries directly to MOM, unsure whether employers had made a report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In the last one year, there were close to 1,900 workers who report their injuries directly to MOM because they were not so sure whether their employers had made a report.

sections.label: Accumulated MC reportable incidents
sections.summary: In 2014 the regulation was changed so accumulated medical leave of three days or more is deemed a reportable incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In 2014, we had decided, and we had changed the regulation, to ensure that even if a doctor gives two days of MC and then have a break in between, and then issues another two days of MC and so on, MOM will still deem all these injuries or MCs as reportable incidents, so long as the accumulative MCs are three days or more.

sections.label: SnapSAFE near-miss reporting app
sections.summary: MOM developed the SnapSAFE mobile app for companies to use as an internal near-miss reporting system, rolled out recently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In that respect, we have developed a mobile app called SnapSAFE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Any company can download this app and use it as their internal reporting system, where their workers or any other employees can report near-misses to the management so as to give the management the opportunity to rectify all the potential risks at the workplace to prevent workplace injuries or fatalities from happening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We have just rolled this out not so long ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: It is premature to talk about whether we want to mandate the companies to adopt near-misses reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: But certainly, we will consider it if the need arises one day.
